Add genomic coordinates in separate columns of a dataframe

mutate_coordinates.Rd

mutate_coordinates is intended to separate genomic coordinates that are listed in a single character string within a dataframe column, which is often the case for copy number variant coordinates, target regions or primer locations. mutate_coordinates also will work when the column contains a mix of single coordinate and paired coordinate strings, which can happen when the locations of different variant types are listed in the same column (such as single nucleotide variants and indels, see example).

Usage

mutate_coordinates(df, coord_col)

Arguments

df

A dataframe

coord_col

The column containing genomic coordinate strings

Value

The dataframe with coordinates extracted into "start" and "end" columns

Examples


test_df <- tibble::tribble(
~"gene", ~"variant", ~"region",
"GENE1", "c.1A>G", "1",
"GENE1", "c.1delATG", "1..3",
"GENE1", "c.123_456dup", "123456789..234567890")

test_df |> mutate_coordinates(coord_col = region)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   gene  variant      region                   start       end
#>   <chr> <chr>        <chr>                    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 GENE1 c.1A>G       1                            1        NA
#> 2 GENE1 c.1delATG    1..3                         1         3
#> 3 GENE1 c.123_456dup 123456789..234567890 123456789 234567890
